notes: Rest-of-word handling: str.title()/capitalize() force the remaining letters to lowercase (HELLO -> Hello, mcDonald -> Mcdonald), while the upper()-only candidates leave them untouched.
Word boundary definition: whitespace-only (hello-world -> Hello-world, it's -> It's) vs any non-word char via title()/\b (Hello-World, It'S, 3Rd, Foo_Bar).
Whitespace normalization: candidate 2 collapses runs/tabs/newlines and strips ends; all others preserve the original whitespace exactly.

Words that start with a non-letter: candidate 5 uppercases the first *letter* inside the token ('quoted' -> 'Quoted', 3rd -> 3Rd); candidate 4 only touches the first character and so leaves them alone.
Empty / whitespace-only input: returned unchanged, collapsed to "" by the split/join variant, or rejected with ValueError by candidate 5.
Unicode case mapping: upper() vs titlecase differ on digraphs and sharp s (ǆemal ß -> Ǆemal SS vs ǅemal Ss).
